why_ai: Bonded contractors build dredged channels, wharves, locks and track on site with heavy floating and land equipment, pricing ground and water risk.
why_clarity: Pay items and specs define the work, but production and margin are known only at closeout, months after the bid.
why_digital: Plans and bid tabs are digital, yet the product is physical infrastructure won through regional public lettings.

why_ai: Dredges, crane barges and pile crews do the work in open water under tides, river stages and environmental windows.
why_clarity: Surveys and specs make deliverables checkable, but every site's water and soil differ and outcomes arrive at closeout.
why_digital: Digital surveys and plans feed work that is entirely physical, bid to the Corps and port owners.

why_ai: Dredges and crews move material on site; low-bid award under a sealed government estimate leaves little relationship protection.
why_clarity: Pay volume comes from before-and-after surveys against a codified prism, repeated across maintenance contracts with quick survey feedback.
why_digital: DQM sensors and surveys are digital, but the work is moving sediment, sold through public dredging lettings.

why_ai: Pile driving and decking over water beside working berths needs crews, cranes and accountable contractors on site.
why_clarity: Pile acceptance and handover dates are checkable, but each wharf's soils and phasing differ.
why_digital: Design and pile records are digital; the structure and the bidding are physical and regional.

why_ai: In-the-wet megaprojects behind cofferdams carry catastrophic, slow-feedback risk that joint ventures must price and control on site.
why_clarity: Specs define the structures, but each project is near one-off and risk outcomes surface over years.
why_digital: Instrumentation and schedules are digital, while the work is mass concrete and earth in a river.

why_ai: Track gangs work on live railroads inside outage windows, with railroad-qualified crews and flaggers on site.
why_clarity: Track feet, turnouts and on-time return of each window are measured immediately and the methods are standard.
why_digital: Window plans are digital, but trackwork is hands-on and contractors are qualified railroad by railroad.

why_ai: Notices and time impact analyses are document work AI can draft, though entitlement is adversarial and a manager signs.

why_digital: Diaries, schedules and contracts in, notices and fragnets out, all on screen for a specific owner.

why_digital: The work is physical shoreline construction sold face to face to local waterfront owners.

why_ai: Crews laser-grade and drain fields and courses on site to tolerances that must pass physical tests.

why_clarity: Item mapping and outlier flags repeat across thousands of lettings and are checked at the next letting.
why_digital: Public bid files in, price histories and flags out, sold remotely to estimators.

why_digital: Site inspections and instrument data feed reports filed digitally with FERC for specific dam owners.

why_clarity: Monthly reports follow a set shape, but whether the diligence was right shows only at completion.
why_digital: Project documents and site visits in, certifications delivered digitally to lenders.

why_ai: Central estimating analytics is screen work, though bid judgement on large risky jobs stays with senior people.
why_clarity: Rate libraries and bid reviews repeat across many bids, and wins and job actuals check them.
why_digital: Estimates and cost data in, rates and reviews out, all on screen inside the firm.

why_digital: Grantee documents in, oversight reports out digitally, bought by one federal agency.

why_ai: Product analytics on customer data is screen work AI-native software can substitute directly.
why_clarity: Benchmarks and features are defined, but their usefulness to estimators is judged slowly.
